## Package map
- @editora/core: web component runtime and framework-agnostic editor APIs.
- @editora/react: React integration for editor runtime.
- @editora/plugins: native plugin packages and presets. Every entry (root, /lite, /enterprise, /<plugin>) tree-shakes, so importing one plugin from the root bundles only that plugin.
- @editora/themes: theming primitives and tokens.
- @editora/ui-core: framework-agnostic UI component library built as custom elements.
- @editora/ui-react: React wrappers around ui-core components.
- @editora/icons and @editora/react-icons: icon packages.
- @editora/toast: notification APIs and primitives. The stylesheet is injected with the first toast, so no CSS import is needed; configure({ nonce }) or <meta property="csp-nonce"> for a CSP. @editora/toast/react: the same toast taking JSX, toast.custom(render), <Toaster />. @editora/toast/lite: no built-in styles (import @editora/toast/toast.css yourself).
- @editora/ui-sortable: drag-and-drop lists and boards. @editora/ui-sortable/headless: createSortable(element, options) for your own markup, plus moveItem / moveBetween / applySortEvent helpers. @editora/ui-sortable/headless/react: useSortable({ items, onChange }) returns { ref }. Keyboard, touch and screen-reader announcements included.
- @editora/markdown-editor: markdown editor for React with live preview.
- @editora/paste-cleaner: cleanPaste({ html, text }) -> { html, source, warnings }; PasteCleanerPlugin from @editora/paste-cleaner/editora.
- @editora/content-a11y: checkContent(html) / fixContent(html); ContentA11yPlugin from @editora/content-a11y/editora; CLI `content-a11y`.
- @editora/ai-review: attachAIReview(element) or AIReviewPlugin from @editora/ai-review/editora; server proxy from @editora/ai-review/server.
- @editora/email-html: toEmailHtml(html, options) -> { html, text, warnings, size }; CLI `email-html`.
- @editora/rich-text-convert: convert(input, { from?, to }) -> { output, warnings }; CLI `rich-text-convert`.
- Content tools docs: https://editora-ecosystem.netlify.app/docs/content-tools/overview

## Coding contract for AI assistants
1. Use concrete imports from @editora/* packages.
2. Keep snippets executable in Vite/React and browser web component setups.
3. Prefer accessible defaults: keyboard support, aria labels, focus states.
4. Respect theme tokens and CSS custom properties for styling.
5. Avoid framework lock-in when the request is framework-agnostic.
6. For UI wrappers, preserve one-to-one mapping with ui-core behavior.

## Output quality constraints
- Include exact import lines.
- Include minimum setup code (mount/root/provider as needed).
- Include configuration as data, not pseudo placeholders.
- Mention required peer/runtime dependencies where relevant.

## Example import patterns
React UI wrappers:
```tsx
import { Button, Dialog, ThemeProvider } from '@editora/ui-react';
import { toastAdvanced } from '@editora/toast';
import { Icon } from '@editora/react-icons';
```

Toasts with JSX (mount <Toaster /> once; plain-text toasts do not need it):
```tsx
import { Toaster, toast } from '@editora/toast/react';
```

Your own sortable list in React:
```tsx
import { useSortable } from '@editora/ui-sortable/headless/react';
const { ref } = useSortable({ items: tasks, onChange: setTasks });
```

Framework-agnostic UI web components:
```html
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@editora/ui-core/dist/index.js"></script>
<ui-button variant="primary">Save</ui-button>
```

Editor with plugins:
```ts
import { createEditor } from '@editora/core';
import { BoldPlugin, MentionPlugin } from '@editora/plugins';
```

Web component: without a plugins attribute the editor loads a small default set (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, clearFormatting, heading, blockquote, list, link, table, history) plus what its toolbar or pluginConfig asks for. Use plugins="all" for every plugin (collaboration stays opt-in):
```html
<editora-editor plugins="all"></editora-editor>
```

## Discovery hints for assistants
- Prefer component metadata from components.json.
- If a component exists in both ui-core and ui-react, ui-core is source-of-truth behavior.
- Use Storybook for visual/state validation and docs for API guarantees.
- `AnimatedNumber` is the React wrapper for `ui-odometer`.
- `AnimatedNumber` supports `odometer`, `inline`, `digital`, and `analog` variants.

## CLI quick-add commands
- npx @editora/cli init (detects the project and framework, asks what to set up, installs it)
- npx @editora/cli add button
- npx @editora/cli add modal
- npx @editora/cli add datatable
- npx @editora/cli add editor
- npx @editora/cli add toast
- npx @editora/cli list [search] [--json] (every name it can add, or a search)
- Supports all exported @editora/ui-react component names (for example: accordion, avatar, select, ui-date-picker).
- Installs with the project's package manager (from packageManager or the lock file), then prints the imports and stylesheet to add.
- Docs: https://editora-ecosystem.netlify.app/docs/reference/cli

## Known intent patterns
- "pixel-perfect" => deliver production-grade visual states and interaction polish.
- "performance" => avoid repeated event listeners, avoid forced sync layout, avoid redundant renders.
- "theme" => expose token overrides and avoid hardcoded colors/radii unless explicitly requested.
